stem: How does nociplastic pain differ from neuropathic and nociceptive pain?

options.text: It involves a direct lesion or disease of the somatosensory nervous system.
It is characterized by central sensitization without evidence of actual or threatened tissue damage.
It is solely the result of activation of nociceptors due to a bone fracture.
It is a psychological condition that does not involve the nervous system.

explanation: Nociplastic pain occurs when there is altered nociception and central sensitization despite no clear damage to tissues or nerves.
rationale: Consider which category explains pain when there is no obvious 'broken' tissue or 'cut' nerve.

optionExplanations.A: This description characterizes neuropathic pain, whereas nociplastic pain occurs without obvious nerve damage.
optionExplanations.B: Nociplastic pain occurs when there is altered nociception and central sensitization despite no clear damage to tissues or nerves.
optionExplanations.C: Pain from a bone fracture is a classic example of nociceptive pain, not nociplastic pain.
optionExplanations.D: While influenced by psychological factors, nociplastic pain is a pathophysiological state of the central nervous system.

source.hint: Consider which category explains pain when there is no obvious 'broken' tissue or 'cut' nerve.
